title: Scouts Guide to the Zombie Apocalypse
sourceTitle: Scouts Guide to the Zombie Apocalypse
synopsis: Your scout troop's overnight camp goes badly when, somehow, half of town becomes flesh-eating. You have a sash, three badges, and a slingshot. Use them.

nodes.text: Saturday morning. Troop leader is missing. Cocoa is cold. You and Carter and Augie find a zombie behind the storage shed. Carter's Plan is already waiting. What changes is whether “Scream” or “Stay quiet” is the instinct you carry into it.

choices.consequence: You scream. The way toward Carter's Plan opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.
You stay quiet. The way toward Carter's Plan opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.

nodes.text: Carter wants to drive to the police station. The police station is, by Augie's count, two miles. Both choices lead to Augie's Sash, but “Walk” arrives there with a different cost than “Bike.” In Carter's Plan, even a sensible delay gives the threat another way in.

choices.consequence: You choose to walk. By Augie's Sash, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.
You commit to bike. It carries you into Augie's Sash while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

nodes.text: Augie has, on his sash, a 'fire-making' badge, a 'first aid' badge, and a 'parade marshal' badge. The last one is, in fact, weirdly useful. Both choices lead to Denise from the Strip Club, but “Use the sash organizationally” arrives there with a different cost than “Mock the sash gently.”

choices.consequence: You commit to use the sash organizationally. It carries you into Denise from the Strip Club while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.
You commit to mock the sash gently. It carries you into Denise from the Strip Club while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

nodes.text: A woman named Denise appears with a baseball bat and saves you from a small mob. She is, immediately, in charge. Both choices lead to Hardware Store, but “Defer to Denise” arrives there with a different cost than “Earn her respect.”

choices.consequence: You commit to defer to Denise. It carries you into Hardware Store while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.
You choose to earn her respect. By Hardware Store, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.

nodes.text: The hardware store has nails, baseball bats, and a single guy named Ron behind the counter who has, apparently, been waiting for this. The road still runs toward The Mall. Its next turn depends on the difference between choosing “Recruit Ron” and choosing “Take supplies and go.”

choices.consequence: You commit to recruit Ron. It carries you into The Mall while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.
You choose to take supplies and go. By The Mall, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.

nodes.text: The mall, of course. Inside is a stage being set up for the high school party tonight. The party may still be on. Half the senior class doesn't know yet. Old People's Home is already waiting. What changes is whether “Warn the party” or “Use the mall to fortify” is the instinct you carry into it.

choices.consequence: You warn the party. The way toward Old People's Home opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.
You use the mall to fortify. The way toward Old People's Home opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.

nodes.text: The retirement home is, surprisingly, mostly fine. The residents have, for various reasons, mistaken the apocalypse for a fire drill. Carter's Crush comes either way; its meaning changes with the difference between “Brief them carefully” and “Leave them; they're safe.”

choices.consequence: You commit to brief them carefully. It carries you into Carter's Crush while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.
You choose to leave them; they're safe. By Carter's Crush, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.

nodes.text: Kendall, Carter's crush, calls his phone. She is at the party. She is, somehow, alive. She is, also, smarter than Carter has ever realized. Zombie Cat will follow either decision, but it will meet a different version of you after “Pivot to the party” than after “Stay on plan.”

choices.consequence: You choose to pivot to the party. By Zombie Cat, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.
You choose to stay on plan. By Zombie Cat, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.

nodes.text: A zombie cat. You both want to laugh and don't. Both choices lead to The High School, but “Distract it” arrives there with a different cost than “Slingshot it.” In Zombie Cat, even a sensible delay gives the threat another way in.

choices.consequence: You distract it. The way toward The High School opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.
You slingshot it. The way toward The High School opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.

nodes.text: The school is locked. The football coach is, weirdly, leading a militia inside. He is, weirdly, doing it well. Slingshot Range will follow either decision, but it will meet a different version of you after “Join the militia” than after “Avoid the militia.”

choices.consequence: You join the militia. The way toward Slingshot Range opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.
You commit to avoid the militia. It carries you into Slingshot Range while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

nodes.text: You have, the badge book says, eighteen inches at minimum for accuracy. You discover, in practice, more like twelve. Augie's Brave Moment will follow either decision, but it will meet a different version of you after “Practice on something static” than after “Use it live.”

choices.consequence: You commit to practice on something static. It carries you into Augie's Brave Moment while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.
You choose to use it live. By Augie's Brave Moment, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.

nodes.text: Augie, who has been the dorkiest of you for nine years, makes a move that saves Denise. The moment is small. The moment is huge. The Trampoline is already waiting. What changes is whether “Make sure he knows” or “Let it be” is the instinct you carry into it.

choices.consequence: You choose to make sure he knows. By The Trampoline, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.
Some bravery is private. You choose to let it be. By The Trampoline, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.

nodes.text: An above-ground pool, a trampoline, two suburban kids' inheritance. You and Carter use them to clear a fence. Mall, Round Two is already waiting. What changes is whether “Catch up to Denise” or “Find Augie first” is the instinct you carry into it.

choices.consequence: You catch up to Denise. The way toward Mall, Round Two opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.
You choose to find Augie first. By Mall, Round Two, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.

nodes.text: The mall stage is up. Half the high school is there. Music is loud. Nobody has noticed the zombies in the food court yet. You cannot avoid Kendall's Smarter; you can only decide whether “Cut the music” or “Lock the doors first” defines the person who reaches it.

choices.consequence: You choose to cut the music. By Kendall's Smarter, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.
You lock the doors first. The way toward Kendall's Smarter opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.

nodes.text: Kendall, faced with the situation, organizes the party into a defense in under two minutes. You realize you have wildly underestimated her. Coach's Militia will follow either decision, but it will meet a different version of you after “Follow her lead” than after “Coordinate as equals.”

choices.consequence: You choose to follow her lead. By Coach's Militia, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.
You choose to coordinate as equals. By Coach's Militia, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.

nodes.text: The coach's militia arrives, late, but timely. Their plan is bad. Your plan is also bad. Together the plans become acceptable. Trampoline Charge will follow either decision, but it will meet a different version of you after “Merge the plans” than after “Stay separate.”

choices.consequence: You merge the plans. The way toward Trampoline Charge opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.
You stay separate. The way toward Trampoline Charge opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.

nodes.text: You orchestrate, against all reason, a trampoline-based charge that picks off the perimeter zombies in a way that, in a different timeline, would have been a YouTube video. Augie's Sash, Again is already waiting. What changes is whether “Commit to it” or “Cover for it tactically” is the instinct you carry into it.

choices.consequence: You commit to it. The way toward Augie's Sash, Again opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.
You choose to cover for it tactically. By Augie's Sash, Again, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.

nodes.text: Augie's parade marshal badge actually saves the entire defensive arrangement by organizing them in a pattern only he knows. Augie, you realize, is the hero of this movie. The Last Wave comes either way; its meaning changes with the difference between “Promote Augie publicly” and “Let him have it quietly.”

choices.consequence: You choose to promote Augie publicly. By The Last Wave, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.
You let him have it quietly. The way toward The Last Wave opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.

nodes.text: Final wave. The football field. The stadium lights are on. You and Carter and Augie and Denise hold the south corner. Kendall holds the north. Both choices lead to Daylight, but “Charge” arrives there with a different cost than “Hold the line.”

choices.consequence: You commit to charge. It carries you into Daylight while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.
You hold the line. The way toward Daylight opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.

nodes.text: Sunrise. The town is, mostly, scoured. The bus carrying the surviving teenagers pulls away. You and Augie sit on the bleachers eating, somehow, leftover pancakes. After School will follow either decision, but it will meet a different version of you after “Celebrate” than after “Sit quietly.”

choices.consequence: You choose to celebrate. By After School, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.
You choose to sit quietly. By After School, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.

nodes.text: Monday morning. School is, weirdly, in session. The town has decided to call this a 'fire' for insurance reasons. The distance between Eagle Scout, Eventually and Kendall and the World begins with the choice between “Stay scouts” and “Quit scouts to be normal.” A third choice, “Take the third path,” keeps Quiet Senior Year in play.

choices.consequence: You choose to stay scouts. By Eagle Scout, Eventually, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.
You commit to quit scouts to be normal. It carries you into Kendall and the World while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.
Some endings reveal themselves last. You choose to take the third path. By Quiet Senior Year, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.

nodes.text: You stay in scouts. You become an Eagle Scout. You write your application essay about the night the trampoline saved a high school. The reviewer, who has heard everything, says it is the most specific essay he has read.

Carter and Kendall become a couple. Augie, somehow, becomes the most popular kid at school. You become the friend who knows. You go on to a normal life that, every Halloween, gets weirder. The road into Kendall and the World began with “Quit scouts to be normal” in After School; here, that decision stops being a moment and becomes a life.
You quietly graduate. You never tell most people the truth about that night. You keep the sash in a box in your closet. Sometimes, late, you take it out and put it on. It still fits.
